instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each employer to file, with the updated registration statement, a statement of expenditures (i.e., the employer's periodic spending report).
Section 101.72(B) requires updated registration statements (with any required expenditure statement) to be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year, which is triannual.
The statute specifies filing in January, May, and September rather than once per year.
Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) are due three times per year, not monthly.
The filing cadence is triannual (January/May/September), not four times per year.
The statute requires three filings per year rather than two.
The statute specifies a triannual cadence and does not prescribe any additional or alternative periodic schedule for employer expenditure statements.
Section 101.73(C) provides that an employer's expenditure statement shall show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer during the period covered.

Expenditures subject to reporting include gifts of anything of value such as food and beverages, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and employer statements report expenditures unless already reported by the agent.
Section 101.73(C) expressly excludes 'the compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of expenditures for employer reporting.

The employer's statement of expenditures under §101.73 requires totals and, if applicable, details of expenditures but does not require listing the names of legislative agents engaged (that information appears in registration statements under §101.72).

When expenditures are made for the benefit of a particular covered official, the statement must provide itemized details including recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client.
The updated registration statement filed with the expenditure statement must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the period.

An initial registration statement must include a brief description of the type of legislation to which the engagement relates, which is a general-issues description included in the periodic filing package.
The employer must file a registration statement giving the employer's name and business address (principal contact info) within ten days of engagement and updated triannually.
The filing required within ten days of engagement must show the legislative agent's name, which identifies the lobbyist.
The initial registration statement must include the legislative agent's business address, providing lobbyist contact information.
The registration statement must include the legislative agent's occupation, which is a statement of business/occupation.
Employer expenditure reporting focuses on expenditures (amounts, descriptions, dates, and related legislation/client) and does not require disclosure of lobbying contacts made.
Section 101.73(C) excludes expenses of maintaining office facilities from reportable expenditures, indicating indirect/overhead costs are not required in employer spending reports.
Neither the registration statement requirements in §101.72 nor the employer expenditure statement requirements in §101.73 require listing any contributors to the employer.
Section 101.72 requires names/addresses of agent and employer, type of legislation, and specific bills/resolutions, but does not require naming bill members or sponsors.
